subject: quantitative_aptitude
question: Walking at (5/6)th of his usual speed, a man reaches his office 15 minutes late. What is his usual time to reach the office?
explanation: Since distance is constant, speed and time are inversely proportional. Speed ratio = 5/6 => Time ratio = 6/5. Let usual time be T. New time = (6/5) T. Delay = (6/5) T - T = (1/5) T. Given delay = 15 minutes: (1/5) T = 15 => T = 75 minutes.

subject: quantitative_aptitude
question: Two athletes run in the same direction on a circular track of circumference 600 meters at speeds of 15 m/s and 25 m/s respectively from the same starting line. After how many seconds from the start will they meet again for the first time at the starting line itself?
explanation: Time taken by Athlete 1 to complete one full lap = 600 / 15 = 40 seconds. Time taken by Athlete 2 to complete one full lap = 600 / 25 = 24 seconds. They will be at the starting line together at multiples of their individual lap times. First meeting at the starting point = LCM(40, 24). Prime factorization: 40 = 2^3 × 5; 24 = 2^3 × 3. LCM = 2^3 × 3 × 5 = 120 seconds.
